what: within-null control: does a no-shift draw's OWN label-prior gap predict its QFC?
why: the C-Mod worked example carries a label-prior shift (0.508475 -> 0.720847) as well as a covariate shift, so a reader can attribute the collapse to class balance. Each no-shift draw splits the source pool 50/50 by shot and therefore carries its own prior gap, with the environment identical by construction.
pre_registered: both outcomes, four forbidden readings and the resolution were fixed before the run, in Desktop/TASK7_PRIOR_GAP_VS_NULL_QFC_PREREGISTRATION.md
reading: The non-parametric half assumes nothing: two draws carry prior gaps LARGER than the real shift's and score z = -0.25 and -0.93 against the floor, where the real comparison scores -2.69. The parametric half bounds it: the relationship is not resolved at n = 30, and the fitted slope puts the prior gap at 18% of the observed drop at the point estimate and 58% at the steep end of its 95% interval -- so the design excludes the prior gap explaining ALL of the drop, leaving at least 42%, but not it explaining some.
limits: One pool, one estimator, thirty draws. The gaps exist because this source pool mixes a 13% prevalence era with a 78% one; another dataset need not, and nothing here says the label prior is irrelevant to QFC in general.
